saints.name: St. Apollonius the Apologist
saints.title: Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A learned Roman senator who defended the faith before the Senate and died for it…
biography: Apollonius was a Roman of rank and learning — a senator, the sources say, and a man versed in philosophy — living under the Emperor Commodus. Denounced as a Christian by one of his own slaves to the praetorian prefect Perennis, he was called upon to answer before the Senate.

There, far from recanting, he read a reasoned defense of Christianity — 'a remarkable volume', Jerome calls it — maintaining that he did not fear death, since eternal life awaits those who have lived well on earth. His judges heard him patiently in two hearings three days apart; but the rescript of Trajan against the Christians stood, and he was condemned to death.

The defense itself, translated into Greek, is lost, though Eusebius preserves the story of his trial in the Ecclesiastical History. He suffered about the year 185 — beheaded, one ancient account says — and stands among the first men of Roman learning to answer persecution with a public and reasoned confession of the faith.
saints.knownFor: His reasoned defense of the faith before the Roman Senate.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain), 18 April
